subject: Accountancy

internalBreakdown.component: Project file (or practical file with Computerised Accounting)

textbooks: Accountancy - Computerised Accounting System, Class XII (NCERT)
notes: Part B is either Financial Statement Analysis (units 3 and 4) or Computerised Accounting (unit CA), 20 marks either way.
Question paper design: remembering and understanding 32 marks, applying 24, analysing, evaluating and creating 24.

chapters.name: Accounting for Partnership: Basic Concepts
topics: Partnership: features, partnership deed
Provisions of the Indian Partnership Act 1932 in the absence of a partnership deed
Fixed versus fluctuating capital accounts
Profit and loss appropriation account: division of profit among partners, guarantee of profits
Past adjustments relating to interest on capital, interest on drawings, salary and profit sharing ratio
outcomes: State the meaning of partnership, partnership firm and partnership deed, and the contents of the deed
Discuss the provisions of the Partnership Act that apply in the absence of a deed
Differentiate fixed and fluctuating capital and prepare the profit and loss appropriation account, including guarantee of profits
Make past adjustments
notes: Interest on partner's loan is treated as a charge against profits.

chapters.name: Goodwill: Nature and Valuation
topics: Goodwill: meaning, nature, factors affecting, need for valuation
Methods of valuation: average profit, super profit and capitalisation
Adjustment through partners' capital or current account
outcomes: State the meaning, nature and factors affecting goodwill
Value goodwill by different methods

chapters.name: Change in Profit Sharing Ratio among Existing Partners
topics: Sacrificing ratio and gaining ratio
Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities; treatment of reserves, accumulated profits and losses
Preparation of revaluation account and balance sheet
outcomes: State the meaning of sacrificing ratio, gaining ratio and change in profit sharing ratio
Prepare the revaluation account and balance sheet on a change in profit sharing ratio

chapters.name: Admission of a Partner
topics: Effect of admission on profit sharing ratio
Treatment of goodwill as per AS 26
Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities; treatment of reserves, accumulated profits and losses
Adjustment of capital accounts; preparation of capital, current account and balance sheet
outcomes: Explain the effect of admission of a new partner on profit sharing ratio
Account for goodwill, revaluation, reserves and capital adjustment and prepare the new firm's balance sheet

chapters.name: Retirement and Death of a Partner
topics: Effect of retirement or death on profit sharing ratio
Treatment of goodwill as per AS 26; revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities
Adjustment of accumulated profits, losses and reserves; adjustment of capital accounts
Preparation of capital, current account and balance sheet; loan account of the retiring partner
Deceased partner's share of profit till the date of death; deceased partner's capital account and executor's account
outcomes: Explain the effect of retirement or death of a partner on profit sharing ratio
Account for goodwill, revaluation, reserves and capital adjustment on retirement or death
Calculate a deceased partner's share till death and prepare the deceased partner's and executor's accounts
Prepare remaining partners' capital accounts and the firm's balance sheet

chapters.name: Dissolution of Partnership Firm
topics: Meaning of dissolution of partnership and of partnership firm; types of dissolution
Settlement of accounts: realisation account, partners' capital accounts and cash or bank account
outcomes: Understand the situations under which a partnership firm can be dissolved
Prepare the realisation account and related accounts
notes: Excluding piecemeal distribution, sale to a company and insolvency of partners.
Tangible assets with no realised value given are taken at book value; intangible assets at nil.
Where realisation expenses are borne by a partner, the question must say how they were paid.

chapters.name: Accounting for Share Capital
topics: Features and types of companies; share and share capital: nature and types
Issue and allotment of equity and preference shares; over and under subscription
Issue at par and at premium; calls in advance and calls in arrears (excluding interest); issue for consideration other than cash
Private placement, Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP), sweat equity
Forfeiture and re-issue of shares
Disclosure of share capital in the company balance sheet
outcomes: Differentiate equity and preference shares and types of share capital
Account for the issue, forfeiture and re-issue of shares
Present share capital in the balance sheet as per Schedule III Part I of the Companies Act 2013

chapters.name: Issue and Redemption of Debentures
topics: Debentures: meaning, types
Issue at par, at a premium and at a discount; issue for consideration other than cash; issue with terms of redemption
Debentures as collateral security: concept
Interest on debentures
Writing off discount or loss on issue of debentures
outcomes: Account for the different categories of debenture issue
Write off discount or loss on issue of debentures
Understand collateral security and its presentation in the balance sheet
Calculate interest on debentures and state the meaning of redemption
notes: Concept of TDS on debenture interest is excluded.
Discount or loss on issue is written off in the year of allotment from Securities Premium (if any), then from the Statement of Profit and Loss as finance cost (AS 16).

chapters.name: Financial Statements of a Company
topics: Meaning, nature, uses and importance of financial statements
Statement of profit and loss and balance sheet in the prescribed form with major headings and sub-headings as per Schedule III to the Companies Act 2013
outcomes: Present the balance sheet with major headings and sub-headings as per Schedule III
notes: Exceptional items, extraordinary items and profit or loss from discontinued operations are excluded.

chapters.name: Tools for Financial Statement Analysis
topics: Financial statement analysis: meaning, significance, objectives, importance and limitations
Tools: comparative statements, common size statements, ratio analysis, cash flow analysis
outcomes: State the meaning, objectives and limitations of financial statement analysis
Prepare comparative and common size statements and explain their uses and differences

chapters.name: Accounting Ratios
topics: Meaning, objectives, advantages, classification and computation
Liquidity ratios: current ratio and quick ratio
Solvency ratios: debt to equity, total asset to debt, proprietary, interest coverage, debt to capital employed
Activity ratios: inventory turnover, trade receivables turnover, trade payables turnover, fixed asset turnover, net asset turnover, working capital turnover
Profitability ratios: gross profit, operating, operating profit, net profit, return on investment
outcomes: Compute and interpret liquidity, solvency, activity and profitability ratios
notes: Net profit ratio is calculated on profit both before and after tax.

chapters.name: Cash Flow Statement
topics: Meaning, objectives, benefits; cash and cash equivalents
Classification of activities
Preparation as per AS 3 (Revised), indirect method only
outcomes: State the meaning and objectives of a cash flow statement
Prepare a cash flow statement by the indirect method as per AS 3
notes: Adjustments relating to depreciation and amortisation, profit or loss on sale of assets including investments, dividend (final and interim) and tax.
Bank overdraft and cash credit are short-term borrowings; current investments are marketable securities unless otherwise specified.
Previous year's proposed dividend is given effect as per AS 4.

chapters.name: Overview of Computerised Accounting System
topics: Application in accounting; features of computerised accounting system
Structure of CAS
Software packages: generic, specific, tailored

chapters.name: Accounting Application of Electronic Spreadsheet
topics: Concept and features of electronic spreadsheet
Generating accounting information: bank reconciliation statement, asset accounting, loan repayment schedule, ratio analysis
Data representation: graphs, charts and diagrams

chapters.name: Using Computerised Accounting System
topics: Installation of CAS, codification and hierarchy of account heads, creation of accounts
Data entry, validation and verification
Adjusting entries, preparation of balance sheet and profit and loss account with closing and opening entries
Need for and security features of the system
